skill.name: cron-schedule-planner
skill.description: Analyzes GitHub Actions cron schedules across repositories, highlights collisions, classifies workload intensity, converts timezones, and suggests less crowded execution times.
skill.summary: Plan GitHub Actions schedules across repositories and reduce resource-heavy job collisions.
skill.author: dboeckli

security_audit.summary: All 98 static alerts are false positives caused by comments, Markdown backticks, escaped formatting, expected command substitution, and benign file handling. Commands use quoted arguments and support the documented read-only analysis. One medium contextual risk remains because repository-controlled values are written unescaped into an agent-facing Markdown report.

remediation.issue: Repository-controlled values are embedded in Markdown without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Escape pipes, line breaks, backticks, and HTML before report generation, then treat the report strictly as untrusted data during summarization.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Remote Data in Agent-Facing Report
semantic_findings.description: Remote workflow names and cron text are inserted into Markdown without escaping. A crafted repository value could alter report structure or inject instructions when an agent summarizes it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script retrieves repository-controlled workflow content and writes derived values directly into Markdown. The downstream instructions explicitly ask an agent to summarize that report.

content.value_statement: Scheduled workflows can collide and increase runner contention. This skill maps cron activity and suggests less crowded times for resource-intensive jobs.
actual_capabilities: Scans scheduled GitHub Actions workflows through the GitHub CLI or local repositories.
Lists cron entries with UTC and current local timezone values.
Classifies workflows as high, medium, or low intensity using documented patterns.
Builds hourly and weekday histograms and identifies crowded UTC hours.
Suggests alternative hours for high-intensity workflows while preserving other cron fields.
Optionally summarizes observed GitHub Actions queue times by UTC hour.
limitations: Cron parsing supports common fixed-hour schedules and labels other expressions as custom.
Intensity classification uses text patterns and can misclassify comments or unusual workflows.
Timezone conversion uses the current date and may differ after daylight-saving changes.
Queue time is a sparse proxy and does not measure GitHub runner capacity directly.

use_cases.title: Reduce CI schedule collisions
use_cases.description: Review scheduled workflows across an organization and move demanding jobs away from crowded hours.

use_cases.title: Coordinate repository maintenance
use_cases.description: Compare nightly builds, dependency updates, and validation jobs before choosing a new schedule.

use_cases.title: Review runner contention
use_cases.description: Combine schedule density with recent queue times to identify practical execution windows.

prompt_templates.title: Check one repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze scheduled workflows in owner/repository and show their UTC and Europe/Zurich times.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a focused schedule inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Find organization collisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan repositories owned by organization and identify crowded UTC hours and high-intensity workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a better build time
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a less crowded hour for the Testcontainers workflow and explain the proposed schedule change.

prompt_templates.title: Use queue evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze organization schedules with recent queue statistics, rank alternative hours, and present changes for approval without editing workflows.

output_examples.output: The report finds three scheduled runs at 02:00 UTC. Two are high-intensity container builds, making this the primary collision window.

output_examples.input: When should the integration build run?
output_examples.output: Move the integration build to an empty UTC hour identified by the report. Review daylight-saving effects before applying the change.

output_examples.input: Are queue delays concentrated at specific times?
output_examples.output: Recent runs show the highest average queue delay during one crowded hour. The suggested alternatives have lower observed delays and no scheduled entries.

best_practices: Use explicit repository scope when only selected projects should be analyzed.
Review suggested times against business deadlines and daylight-saving changes.
Confirm every workflow edit after inspecting the generated report and proposed difference.
anti_patterns: Do not treat pattern-based intensity labels as exact resource measurements.
Do not assume queue delays are caused only by runner contention.
Do not apply schedule changes automatically without repository owner approval.

faq.question: Does the skill edit workflow files?
faq.answer: No. The script produces recommendations, and workflow changes require explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it scan private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, when the authenticated GitHub CLI account has access to those repositories.

faq.question: Can it work without GitHub API access?
faq.answer: Yes. Local mode scans workflow files in local repository checkouts.

faq.question: How are intensive workflows identified?
faq.answer: Documented text patterns detect containers, clusters, matrix builds, Maven, Gradle, and Docker image builds.

faq.question: Are local times daylight-saving aware?
faq.answer: Conversion uses the current date. Future schedules may shift after a daylight-saving transition.

faq.question: What do queue statistics represent?
faq.answer: They summarize delays between creation and start times for recent runs. They are an indirect and sometimes sparse contention signal.
